# SOC 2 Type I Report Summary

**Report issued:** 2026-06-30 by Ledgerwise Assurance · **Point-in-time date:** 2026-05-31 · **Opinion:** Unqualified (clean) · **Observations:** 2

This is an internal summary. The full report is in the restricted SOC 2 folder; share it externally only under NDA and with Maya Chen's approval. Program context: SOC 2 Program Overview.

## What a Type I says

The auditor checked that our controls were **designed** appropriately and **in place** on 2026-05-31. It does not test whether they operated over time; that's the Type II, whose observation window runs 2026-07-01 to 2026-12-31.

## Scope

- Criteria: Security and Availability.
- System description: Stencil's consumer savings platform, including the Rails monolith, Go money movement services, production AWS, and supporting tooling.
- Carve-outs: AWS, Pillar Bank, Plaid, Alloy and DriveWealth are subservice organizations; we rely on their own reports.

## Results

- 58 controls tested for design and implementation.
- 0 exceptions.
- 2 observations (not exceptions; the auditor's advice on things likely to cause Type II exceptions if left alone).

### Observation 1: change management on money-movement code

In a sample of 25 production changes, 3 changes to money-movement code had one approving reviewer instead of the two our Code Review Standards require. All 3 were emergency merges; the policy allows post-merge review within 24 hours but there was no record that the post-merge review happened.

Response (Marcus Bell): a merge check now requires two approvals on protected paths, and emergency merges open a follow-up ticket automatically, closed only when a second reviewer approves.

### Observation 2: offboarding timeliness

One contractor's Datadog account was removed 6 days after their engagement ended. Policy is 1 business day. This is the same pattern as the GitHub contractor gap in Security Review - Quarterly 2026-Q1. The automated offboarding workflow covers SSO apps but Datadog had a local account.

Response (Sam): all Datadog users moved to SSO-only; quarterly access review now includes a check for local accounts on every system.

## Subservice organization reports we reviewed

| Vendor | Report | Period | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| AWS | SOC 2 Type II | Current | Standard |
| Pillar Bank | SOC 1 Type II | Current | Bank reports through their auditor |
| Plaid | SOC 2 Type II | Current | |
| Alloy | SOC 2 Type II | Current | Formal vendor risk assessment still to do |
| DriveWealth | SOC 1 and SOC 2 Type II | Current | Formal vendor risk assessment still to do |

## What this means for the Type II

Decision: we treat both observations as if they were findings and track the fixes to closure before 2026-07-31, so the Type II sample starts clean.

Risk: the Type II tests operation over six months. Anything that works in May but slips in a busy quarter (access reviews during a launch, for example) shows up as an exception.

## Follow-ups

- [x] Marcus: enforce two approvals on money-movement paths and auto-open post-merge review tickets by 2026-07-15
- [x] Sam: move Datadog to SSO-only and remove local accounts by 2026-07-10
- [x] Sam: add local-account checks to the Access Review Procedure by 2026-07-08
- [x] Maya: share the Type I with Pillar Bank (Priya Shah) under NDA by 2026-07-02
